items.excerpt: Portuguese auteur Edgar Pera discusses 'Asphalt Guerrilla,' premiering at Locarno, which blends fact, fiction and AI-generated imagery into a story about filmmaking. He explains how he uses AI as a craft tool precisely to argue against it.

Warner Bros. built a campaign for the Anne Hathaway/Ewan McGregor sci-fi film 'The End of Oak Street' around an AI-generated talking-dog podcast. A studio marketing department using generative video as a first-class promo format, not a test.

Asteria, the AI studio co-founded by Bryn Mooser and Natasha Lyonne, has struck a strategic partnership with virtual production studio ZeroSpace. The deal pairs Asteria's clean-trained generative models with ZeroSpace's stage, mocap and volumetric capture pipeline.

Locarno Pro industry head Markus Duffner frames this year's program around 'power, people, data' — AI, algorithms and consolidation versus creative freedom. A read on how European independent cinema is organizing its response to generative tools.

Gregg Araki, no fan of AI, describes the one place it earned its keep on 'I Want Your Sex': a specific editing problem he could not solve any other way. A concrete craft account rather than a position statement.

Bob Gaudette and Kirk Hipkiss launched Nolia, a Toronto AI film and TV studio built around original IP, with 'The Little Cloud Thief' in development as feature and series. Gaudette's 8-minute short took the $50K Grand Prix at this year's Runway AI Festival.

A Disney SEC filing names ILM and Pixar in the company's machine-learning push, with money behind Disney Research Studios and Imagineering and a pledge that the creative process stays 'human-centered.' It lands after job reductions at Pixar earlier this year.

Toby Lockerbie explains how self-taught animation and VFX built Epic Spaceman into one of YouTube's top science channels — and why genAI has no place in his pipeline. A working counter-case on craft economics at solo scale.

Wonder Dynamics co-founders Tye Sheridan and Nikola Todorovic explain how their filmmaking backgrounds shaped the design of AI production tools for artists. A tool-maker interview about where the human control surfaces belong.

Rich Young's monthly After Effects roundup covers the beta AI Assistant that automates physics animation and layer management via natural language, plus the third-party AI tools reshaping motion work. A survey of what actually shipped into AE this month.

Roku has launched Fairground, a free ad-supported channel of fully AI-generated programming, and the viewing experience is grim. An early read on what happens when generative video is scheduled as linear television.
Curious Refuge tests NVIDIA's world model and argues it points past prompt-to-clip toward navigable, consistent scene space. Framed for filmmakers deciding what to learn next.

A shot-by-shot breakdown of an AI short the channel rates as a genuine artistic success, tracing the directing choices rather than the model list. Craft analysis of what separates a good AI film from a demo reel.
